title: Preservation under clearing a register
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with oracle, input $x$, guard $G$, and a register configuration $(v,	ext{none})$, where $v$ assigns a natural number to each of the $m$ registers. Suppose the instruction at state $l$ deterministically clears register $r$ and moves to state $l'$, and suppose $G$ holds at $(l,v,	ext{none})$. If the program started at $l'$ with register $r$ set to $0$, all other register values unchanged, and no recorded answer has the property that it terminates with guard $G$ and, for every run length at which all choice sequences halt, has probabilities $p$ and $1-p$ of answering true and false, respectively. Then the program started at $l$ with configuration $(v,	ext{none})$ has that same property.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at state $l$ is the deterministic clearing of register $r$ followed by a move to $l'$
From $l'$ with register $r$ set to $0$, the program satisfies the stated termination and output-probability property for $p$
